full_judgment:
2. Shorn of unnecessary details, fact of the case lies in a very short compus. The opposite party No. 1, as plaintiff, filed Partition Suit No. 58 of 1999 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Rangunia, Chattogram, against the present petitioner, along with others as defendants, for a decree of partition. 

 3. The.petitioners as defendant Nos. 2 and 3 filed written statement in the suit. Thereafter, in usual course, the suit was fixed on 30-1-2002 for peremptory hearing. On the date fixed the plaintiff filed hajira, but the defendants did not file hazira even took any step on their behalf. When the matter was taken up for hearing, the defendants and their learned Advocate were found absent on repeated calls. Consequently, the trial court took the matter for ex-parte hearing, recorded evidence of the plaintiff as PW 1 and decreed the suit. Thereafter, the defendants filed Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure ("Code") on 29-2-2012 and the same was dismissed for default on 28-11-2012. The petitioners filed an application under section 151 of the Code on the same date praying for restoration of the miscellaneous case, the court allowed the same and restored the case. Thereafter, miscellaneous case was rejected on merit by judgment and order dated 23-1-2013. After rejection of the miscellaneous case, the defendants preferred Partition Appeal No. 57 of 2013 before the District Judge, Chattogram on 13-3-2013 against the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 30-1-2012 passed in Partition Suit No. 58 of 1999 at a delay of 371 days with an application for condonation of such delay. The appellate court heard the matter and upon hearing disallowed the appeal by its impugned judgment dated 14-3-2013 being barred by limitation. 

 5. Mr Md Anowarul Islam, learned Advocate appearing for the Petitioners, submits that the petitioners in their application for condonation of delay clearly stated that the appellants being wrong advised by their learned Advocate filed miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code for setting aside the decree instead of filing appeal against the ex-parte decree passed by the trial court and in pursuing the said miscellaneous case, there has been a delay of 371 days in filing the appeal. As such, the appellate court ought to have considered the application for delay, but it did not do so. He further submits that before passing an ex-parte decree, the court is required to go through the records, evidence of the plaintiff and to discuss the evidences atleast at the minimum, but in the instant case the trial court in passing ex-parte decree did not even discussed a single evidence both oral and documentary. As such, the ex-parte judgment and decree passed by the trial court cannot stand good. The appellate court utterly failed to consider the grounds taken in the appeal memo, as such, committed error of law occasioning failure of justice. In support of his submissions he has referred to the case of Alfu Miah and others vs Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 1993 (1) BLT (AD) page 25 = 45 DLR (AD) 112. 

 6. Mr M Belayet Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that the petitioners, as defendant in suit, failed to appear before the court on the date fixed for hearing. Consequently, the suit was decreed ex-parte and thereafter, the defendants rightly filed Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the ex-parte decree. 

 7. The said miscellaneous case also dismissed for default on 28-11-2012 and again restored on the prayer of the petitioners and finally on merit the case was rejected by the trial court on 23-1-2013. He further submits that the petitioners have had opportunity to prefer appeal against the judgment and order dated 23-1-2013 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012, but the petitioners instead of preferring appeal against the judgment and order passed in the miscellaneous case, preferred appeal against ex-parte decree dated 30-1-2012 before the learned District Judge at a delay of 371 days. As such, the appellate court rightly rejected the application for condonation of delay and dismissed the appeal being barred by limitation holding that from the very date of passing ex-parte decree, the appellants were fully aware about the judgment passed by the trial court. 

 8. He further submits that once a defendant filed miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code praying for setting aside an ex-parte decree and the same is disposed of with an order of rejection. The petitioner is to prefer appeal against such order and they cannot prefer appeal against the ex-parte decree passed by the trial court by passing and or giving a go bye to the proceeding under Order IX, rule 13 and the order thereof, as such, the rule is liable to be discharged. In support of his submissions he has referred to a catena of cases Badvel Chinna Asethu and others vs Vettipalli Kesavayya and another reported in AIR 1920 Madras 962, Harishbhai Chunilal Shah vs Nalinkumar Champaklal Shah and others reported in AIR 1995 Gujarat 197 and M/s Mangilal Rungta, Calcutta vs Manganese Ore (India) Ltd. reported in AIR 1987 Bombay 87. 

 10. Opposite party No. 1 instituted Partition Suit No. 58 of 1999 on 28-7-1999 in the court of Assistant Judge, Rangunia, Chattogram for a decree of partition of only 21,2 sataks property mentioned in schedule "1(1(a)" to the plaint. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were contesting the suit by filing written statement. Among other dates the suit was fixed for hearing on 30-1-2012. On the date fixed the defendants did not file hazira even took any step on their behalf. The trial court took up the matter in the absence of the defendants and heard the same ex-parte and passed the judgment and decree in preliminary form. Thereafter, present petitioner filed an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code on 29-2-2012 for setting aside the decree, which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012. The said miscellaneous case was contested by the opposite party No. 1 and after hearing, the trial court by its judgment and order dated 23-1-2013 rejected the same holding that there are no sufficient cause for not appearing before the court on the date of hearing of the suit. And also held that the defendants were trying to delay the disposal of the suit by filing several applications for adjournment. Thereafter, the defendant-petitioner did not move before any higher court against the judgment and order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012 and without taking any appeal against the judgment and order passed in miscellaneous case, the defendants preferred an appeal being No. 57 of 2013 against the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 30-1-2012 passed in Partition Suit No. 58 of 1999 before the District Judge at a delay of 371 days. Learned District Judge took up the matter for hearing and upon hearing by the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-3-2013 dismissed the appeal being barred by limitation hence, the present revision. 

 11. Now the question before this Court, whether a defendant after taking recourse to Order IX, rule 13 of the Code by filing an application praying for setting aside an ex-parte decree can again agitate the ex-parte decree by filing a regular appeal before the appellate court. The Law of Civil Procedure, by Mahmudul Islam, volume 1, 2009 at page 376 and the case Harishbhai Chunilal Shah vs Nalinkumar Champaklal Shah and others reported in AIR 1995 Gujarat 197 clearly held that; 

 12. It is quite obvious that the defendants sought to have an ex-parte decree set-aside, by filing an application specifically contemplated and permissible under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code. This application was, therefore, statutory remedy available to the defendants. In pursuing this remedy it cannot be suggested that the other remedy available to the party, like appeal before the appellate court was suspended or that the same could be exercised at some later point on time in case the proceeding under Order IX, rule 13 failed, there is absolutely, no such proposition in law. 

 13. The defendants had two options to seek relief against the ex-parte decree; one is, by filing an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code and other is an appeal under section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the appellate court. In the instant case, the defendants rightly availed of the proceeding for getting the ex-parte decree set-aside by filing an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code. The said case when dismissed by the court below, only option remained open for the applicants to agitate the matter before the appellate court by filing an appeal against the judgment and order passed by the trial court rejecting the application filed by the defendants praying for setting aside the ex-parte decree. But the petitioners did not file any appeal against the rejection order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012, under section 104 read with Order 43 rule 1(b) of the Code, but filed an appeal against the ex-parte decree passed in Partition Suit No. 58 of 1999 at a delay of 371 days. The appellate court rightly rejected the appeal on the ground of limitation. In the application for condonation of delay, the petitioners stated that the delay was caused because of pursuing the statutory remedy by filing a miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 of the code. It is in this Court's view that such contention of the petitioners do not constitute sufficient cause for condonation of delay. 

 16. Consequently, this Court finds no merit in the Rule. However, the petitioners may agitate the judgment and order dated 30-1-2013 passed by the trial court in Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2012 before the appellate court seeking condonation of delay on the ground of consuming time in pursuing the appeal against the ex-parte decree, if so advised and not otherwise barred by any law.
